messages:
Maria Karp: Quick postmortem synthesis from today's DR event — consolidating owners for playbook updates and timelines. TL;DR: snapshot validation intermittently failed in us-east-2 and Route53 failover TTL mismatch amplified switchover latency. Please read and ack.
Sam Li: Ack. I'll own the Route53/check-and-enforce TTL automation. Plan: add an infra healthcheck that verifies failover TTL == 60s, plus a CI gate. ETA: 2025-05-02. @Lee Park can you add this to runbook checklist?
Ana Gomez: I'll take backup/validation. Current script does s3 ls + size checks; I'll add manifest+sha256 verification and an alert if any manifest mismatch. Target: 2025-04-30. Will open a draft PR today.
Devon Shah: I'll convert the restore steps into a runnable runbook (runbooks/restore-regional.md) and add explicit rollback points. Also suggest a compact "mini game day" run monthly to exercise restores — low-customer-impact region. Who should run the first rehearsal?
Lee Park: Monthly mini game day works. I can slot the first one for the second Wed in May and coordinate on-call coverage. Will create a calendar invite and a checklist template.
Olivia Chen: One more pattern we noticed — cache priming caused a long tail during failover (cold KV caches). Propose adding a cache-warm step to the runbook and an automated prefix rehydrate job post-failover. I'll prototype a proof-of-concept.
Sam Li: Example snippet to add to runbook for ALB healthcheck verification:
```bash
# health check
curl -sS https://<region>-api.redwood.ai/health | jq -r '.ok'
# expect: "true"
``` 
Add this as a gating step before marking region as healthy again.
incident-bot: Incident 1905559876 recorded. Postmortem draft: https://redwood-internal/postmortems/1905559876. Affected subset: 0.7% of hosted API traffic in us-east-2. (automated note)
Maria Karp: Consolidated action items (short):
- Route53 TTL enforcement + infra check -> Owner: Sam Li -> ETA: 2025-05-02
- Backup manifest + sha256 verification -> Owner: Ana Gomez -> ETA: 2025-04-30
- Restore runbook -> Owner: Devon Shah -> ETA: 2025-05-06
- Mini game day (monthly) coordination -> Owner: Lee Park -> First run: 2025-05-14
- Cache rehydrate prototype -> Owner: Olivia Chen -> ETA: 2025-05-09
Please react with :thumbsup: to acknowledge or reply if you need a different ETA.
Ana Gomez: :thumbsup: I pushed the initial PR outline, link in thread. Will add CI test that simulates a partial manifest mismatch.
Devon Shah: I'll draft the runbook doc today and include a short play: "Restore from snapshot -> preflight validation -> DNS change -> cache rehydrate -> traffic shift monitor". Will add a clear rollback command block.
Sam Li: Also proposing a small automation: nightly snapshot validation job (runs once, verifies manifests for last 3 snapshots). Cron idea: `0 03 * * * /opt/scripts/validate_snapshots.sh --recent 3` — alerts to #eng-sre if mismatch. Thoughts?
Olivia Chen: Love the nightly check. Can we gate it to run only on primary region to reduce noise? If so, add a flag. I'll coordinate.
Lee Park: I'll draft a short postmortem action-tracker doc (spreadsheet) with owners, status, and verification steps. Will share link in #incidents and set fortnightly check-ins until all closed.
Maria Karp: Good. One more note: look for recurring patterns in last 6 months — snapshot hash failures showed up twice with slightly different causes. @Ana Gomez and @Devon Shah please add a root-cause consolidation section in the postmortem doc so we can decide if we need infra changes vs process changes.
Sam Li: FYI — I'll also add a small Route53 rollback snippet to the runbook so on emergency we can revert TTLs and DNS records quickly. Example: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://rollback.json`.
incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: mini game day invite created by Lee Park for 2025-05-14. (automated)
Maria Karp: Thanks everyone. If you change owners/ETAs update the tracker. We'll review progress in next incident scrum. :eyes:
